subject: literature
passage: When the results of the 800-meter race were announced, Tobias had finished fourth, one place short of a medal. He shook hands with the winner, smiled for his teammates, and told his coach that he felt fine. But on the bus ride home, he sat alone in the back row, staring out the window, and did not answer when his best friend asked if he wanted to play cards. These details suggest that Tobias ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: was pleased with his result but too tired to talk.
choices.B: was angry at the winner for beating him unfairly.
choices.C: did not care at all how he had done in the race.
choices.D: was more disappointed than he had shown others.

explanation.why: In public, Tobias shook hands, smiled, and said he felt fine. Later, alone on the bus, he stared out the window and ignored his friend. The contrast suggests that his calm behavior hid real disappointment about missing a medal.
explanation.A: Incorrect. His silence and isolation on the bus suggest unhappiness, not pleasure with his result.
explanation.B: Incorrect. He shook hands with the winner, and nothing suggests he thought the race was unfair.
explanation.C: Incorrect. His withdrawn behavior on the bus shows that the result did matter to him.
explanation.D: Correct. His cheerful public behavior contrasts with his silence later, showing hidden disappointment.
